record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Y be a smooth, strictly convex planar billiard table, and let Φ be the annular phase space of its billiard map φ. An invariant circle is a φ-invariant noncontractible topological circle Γ⊂Φ, and Y is called integrable when the union of invariant circles in Φ has nonempty interior. Is every such integrable billiard table necessarily an ellipse?

evidence.quote: Definition 1. A billiard table Y is integrable if the union of invariant circles in the phase space has nonempty interior.
Problem 1. Ellipses are the only integrable billiard tables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth, strictly convex bounded planar domain, regarded as a billiard table. The associated billiard map $\varphi$ acts on the annular phase space $\Phi = \partial Y \times (0,\pi)$, where a point $(q,\theta) \in \Phi$ represents a unit tangent vector based at $q \in \partial Y$ making angle $\theta$ with the positively oriented tangent line to $\partial Y$ at $q$; the map $\varphi$ sends $(q,\theta)$ to the corresponding data at the next point of reflection, with the standard reflection law (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). An invariant circle is a $\varphi$-invariant noncontractible topological circle $\Gamma \subset \Phi$. Say that $Y$ is integrable if the union of all invariant circles in $\Phi$ has nonempty interior. 

Prove or disprove: every integrable smooth strictly convex planar billiard table is an ellipse.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Birkhoff conjecture on integrable planar billiards. It remains open in full generality. Significant partial progress includes the Bialy theorem (if the entire phase space is foliated by invariant circles, the table is a disk), Mather's results, the Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin result for rationally integrable tables near a circle, and the Kaloshin–Sorrentino local proof of the conjecture for perturbations of ellipses of small eccentricity. The general conjecture is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards (Kaloshin–Sorrentino)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove a local version of Birkhoff conjecture, namely that any sufficiently smooth domain close to an ellipse of small eccentricity that is integrable is an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Only a local version near ellipses of small eccentricity is proved; the global Birkhoff conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: An integrable deformation of an ellipse of small eccentricity is an ellipse
status_evidence.snippet: Annals of Mathematics paper proving the local Birkhoff conjecture for small-eccentricity ellipses.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms only local resolution; full conjecture open.
